clue.text: Running eccentric kind of swindle

indicators.note: running here means set in motion and churned about, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd variety of fraud is being carried out by some eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like it describes the swindle in progress, but it is the anagram signal for all three words 'eccentric kind of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A con game in which the victim's trust is won and then exploited is a classic kind of swindle.

clue.text: Spooner's pawned pet for something to wear

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first letters of the two synonyms trade places

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: Someone has pawned the family pet to buy something to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered hat with the brim turned up is a type of headgear, so something you wear.

clue.text: Scrooge briefly pulling up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: pulling something along is dragging it

explanation.surface: Scrooge is being pulled up short, perhaps reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final G from DRAGGING to get DRAGGIN, then 'up' reads it backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, Dickens's miser, has become a byword for a stingy person, a tight-fisted miser.

clue.text: Shame of short little chap, embraced by couple extremely naughtily

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the shortened little chap sits within the other letters

parts.note: a couple is two, II in Roman numerals

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the synonym is lopped off

parts.note: a gnome is a little man of folklore

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: A small man is being cuddled by a pair behaving rather naughtily, which is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a verb but gives the Roman numeral for two; 'embraced by' sets the shortened little chap between those two Is, ahead of the ends of 'naughtily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Public disgrace or dishonour is a synonym for shame.

clue.text: Perhaps unknown port in African country

parts.note: perhaps signals an example, abbreviated eg
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A port of uncertain identity is said to be somewhere in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation on the Nile in north-east Africa is a country of that continent.

clue.text: Student pass many picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase built is said aloud

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass and a legion means many, giving col plus legion

explanation.surface: A student passes, with many others listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: COL (pass) and LEGION (many) together are said aloud to sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member or student of a college is a scholar there, so a student.

clue.text: It's semaphore, of course

parts.note: the bookmakers' hand-signalling system used at racecourses is a semaphore of the course, while 'of course' pretends to mean naturally

explanation.surface: Someone states the obvious: this is semaphore, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the arm-waving code British bookmakers use at racecourses to pass on betting odds; 'of course' means of the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The bookies' arm-signalling code is literally a semaphore of the racecourse.

clue.text: Daughters lost to dice and drink in place where blades are used

indicators.note: lost to means taken away from, so the letters for daughters vanish from the two words

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two daughters are DD

explanation.surface: Daughters have been lost to gambling and drink, in the dens where knives come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from 'dice' and the D from 'drink' to leave ICE and RINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates have blades, and a skating arena is where they are put to use.

clue.text: Woman scrubbing edges of most floors

parts.note: Kay is a woman's name

indicators.note: scrubbing edges of means the outer letters of the next word are rubbed away

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman scrubs the edges of most of the floors.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone out in boxing, a KO, is to floor them; the plural verb matches 'floors'.

clue.text: Strength of company data starts to convince you

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information or data

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A firm's figures help to begin persuading you of its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The forcefulness of an argument is its persuasive power or strength.

clue.text: Church stopping dubious sexual activity

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: leery means wary or dubious

explanation.surface: The church is putting a stop to some questionable goings-on of a sexual kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive lust, and the lewd behaviour it leads to, is a form of sexual activity.

clue.text: Her pa heads off for a time

indicators.note: heads off means the first letter of each word is removed

explanation.surface: Her father is heading off for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch is a period, a span of time.

clue.text: Summer activity?

parts.note: a summer here is one who sums, doing arithmetic, not the warm season

explanation.surface: A question about what to do in the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Summer' as someone who adds up numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out sums is the business of the science of number, so it is what an adder does.

clue.text: Noticed his revelling is devoted to pleasure

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild partying, so the letters cavort into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a man's partying shows him to be a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the philosophy that pleasure is the highest good lives a life devoted to enjoyment.

clue.text: Doggedly continue what ironmonger did, conserving energy

indicators.note: conserving means keeping something within, so one letter is held inside the phrase

parts.note: an ironmonger sold iron
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Keep going, as the hardware dealer did while saving energy.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLD IRON with E tucked in after SOLDI gives SOLDI-E-RON.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere stubbornly in spite of difficulty is to keep going doggedly.

clue.text: Ladies' fingers and thumbs up Rihanna's clothes

parts.note: a thumbs-up signals OK, approval

indicators.note: clothes here means the outer covering of the name, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Women's fingers give a thumbs-up to the singer Rihanna's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' fingers' is the British name for the vegetable; the outer letters of Rihanna are R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pods of this vegetable are commonly called ladies' fingers in Britain and India.

clue.text: They burn croissants, scraping off carbon vigorously

indicators.note: vigorously suggests energetic stirring, so the remaining letters are churned into a new order
scraping off means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Bakers burn the pastries and scrape the charred bits off energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C from CROISSANTS leaves ROISSANTS, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raisers who deliberately set property alight are people who burn things.

clue.text: Discard port, subject to legal constraints

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
Dover is an English Channel port

explanation.surface: A port is abandoned because of legal restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: To bind someone over is a British court order requiring them to keep the peace; 'subject' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order obliging someone to keep the peace places them under legal restraint.

clue.text: Revolutionary from the Right is wrong

indicators.note: from the right means read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: Trot is short for a Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A political claim that a revolutionary from the right wing is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' pretends to be the political wing but is the direction of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a civil wrong for which damages can be claimed is called by this name.

clue.text: Novel cocktail of beer and cocoa, but no eggs

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up
but no means the following letters are left out

parts.note: an O looks like an egg, so eggs are OO

explanation.surface: A strange drink mixing beer and cocoa, minus the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER plus COCOA without its two Os leaves BEERCCA, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier wrote a famous novel of that title, so it is a book.

clue.text: Flatters dull single females

parts.note: bland means dull or insipid
I is the Roman numeral for one, single
shes are female people or animals

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talks some unexciting unattached women.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax with flattery is to cajole; the plural verb matches 'flatters'.

clue.text: Dog returned, holding letter and pen

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the letter goes inside
returned means sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a pooch is a dog
en is the name of the printing letter N

explanation.surface: A dog has been brought back, carrying a letter and a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure; 'letter' is the printer's spelt-out name for N, which 'holding' places after the first letter of the reversed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for poultry is a pen for hens.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon supporting angry cry: "Greece for the Greeks!"

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the abbreviation follows

parts.note: Hell! is an angry exclamation

explanation.surface: A furious nationalist protest shouting that Greece belongs to the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellas is the Greek people's own name for their country.

clue.text: Idealistic, bone idle male seething in discontented netherworld

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the outer pair
discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving just the outer letters
seething means churning, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unhappy underworld where a lazy man seethes, yet he has lofty ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: Having high moral principles and lofty aims is to be high-minded, idealistic.

clue.text: Bouquets of new flowers right away

indicators.note: away means removed, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: roses are flowers

explanation.surface: Bunches of fresh flowers sent off at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquets' means the aromas of wine, not bunches of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's aroma is its bouquet, and wine tasters call it the nose.

clue.text: Clobber Doctor Seuss, gutted about end of tale

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the next word
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Attacking the children's author Dr Seuss, sickened by how a story ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothing, not a verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British for clothes or gear, which is what this garment word means.

clue.text: Sister, in turn, nipped out regularly

indicators.note: nipped out regularly means every other letter is pinched out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A sister, in her turn, slipped out at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious sister is a woman in a holy order.

clue.text: Cryptic clues are mostly profane

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are scrambled
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A grumble that crossword clues are generally irreverent.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane in the sense of non-religious, worldly rather than sacred, means the same as this word.

clue.text: Nice solvers hug Arachne on edges of Edmonton Green

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the hugging piece comes after the edge letters
edges of means the first and last letters of the word
hug means embrace, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in Nice, in France, you solvers would be addressed as vous
the setter Arachne refers to herself as I

explanation.surface: Crossword fans in Nice cuddle the setter near the edges of a green in Edmonton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective. Edmonton Green is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green with envy is a stock idiom, so green means covetous.

clue.text: During marvellous tar sands trip espied colours of America

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the answer is found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: On a wonderful trip to the tar sands, someone spotted the American flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag of the United States is its national colours, nicknamed for its emblems.
